name: Your Asset
about: What it is and what is in it, in plain words: how many models, which formats, the poly count, the palette. 2000 characters.

files.name: your-asset.glb
files.sha256: the 64 hex characters sha256sum prints for your-asset.glb

_id: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', up to 48 characters. An id belongs to the first repo that publishes it, so a fork picks its own.
_kind: One of: model, texture, material, sprite, tileset, animation, sound, music, font, shader, ui, vfx, plugin, template, pack, other.
_license: Required: an SPDX id like CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 or MIT, or "custom" with a LICENSE file in this repo.
_engines: The engines it is built for; "any" means plain files that fit anywhere. A file may name one engine ("engine": "godot") and is then installed only for it.
_price_cents: 0 to 99. A priced asset installs only for a wallet that holds its licence. Add "payee": "0x…" to be paid; until then the gamedev wallet holds what it earns.
_files: 1 to 16 files. Each url is a release asset of THIS repo: https://github.com/<you>/<this repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>. size is in bytes. `elo assets init <folder> --repo … --tag …` writes this list for you.
_optional: preview (a .png or .jpg committed in this repo), tags, credit (the line a game prints; we write one if you leave it out), source (an https link to where the work came from, when it is not all yours), payee, made_with (where a model was used: parts from art, code, audio, writing, translation, qa; an empty list means none) and requires (other asset ids).
_next: Upload the files to a GitHub release on a public repo, commit this file at the repo's root as elo-asset.json, then paste the repo at https://elopros.com/assets.html, run `elo assets publish --repo https://github.com/you/your-asset`, or POST https://elopros.com/api/assets/publish with {"repo": "https://github.com/you/your-asset"}. For an update, make a new release, change version and the files, commit, and publish again. Keys starting with _ are your own notes and are ignored.
